summary: The Amalfi Coast is a breathtaking stretch of Italian coastline featuring dramatic cliffs, pastel-colored villages clinging to hillsides, and world-class Mediterranean cuisine. A UNESCO World Heritage site offering stunning photography, coastal hikes, and the best fresh seafood and limoncello in Italy. Perfect for romance, culinary adventures, and capturing some of Europe's most iconic landscapes.

restaurants.name: Da Salvatore
restaurants.description: Family-run trattoria in Amalfi serving traditional Campania cuisine with fresh pasta and local fish daily. Locals fill this modest restaurant for authentic flavors and generous portions.

restaurants.name: L'Antica Trattoria
restaurants.description: Cozy spot in Positano with sea views and Mediterranean comfort food made from local ingredients. Known for their handmade pasta and fresh mozzarella.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Pappalardo
restaurants.description: Elegant clifftop restaurant overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea with innovative takes on classic Amalfi dishes. Michelin-recognized for exceptional service and presentation.
restaurants.mustTry: Sea urchin ravioli with champagne sauce

restaurants.name: Pizza Vertigo
restaurants.description: Casual pizzeria in Positano serving wood-fired Neapolitan pizza at reasonable prices. Perfect for quick, delicious lunch with a view.
restaurants.mustTry: Pizza Amalfi with fresh mozzarella and local herbs

restaurants.name: Il Tram
restaurants.description: Historic lemon-themed restaurant in Amalfi town featuring dishes and drinks infused with the famous local lemons. Try their signature limoncello and lemon pasta.

restaurants.name: Casa Costagliola
restaurants.description: Sophisticated dining in Ravello with terraced sea views and chef-driven Mediterranean cuisine using organic local produce. Multi-course tasting menus showcase seasonal ingredients.
restaurants.mustTry: Lobster with fresh passion fruit and basil

restaurants.name: Ristorante Giordano
restaurants.description: Long-established restaurant in Praiano with a small terrace overlooking the sea and specializing in fresh daily catches. Known for their warm hospitality and simple, well-executed dishes.

restaurants.name: Café Pasticceria
restaurants.description: Charming café throughout the coast towns offering fresh pastries, espresso, and casual lunch. Perfect for breakfast before exploring or taking a break during the day.

restaurants.name: Aurora
restaurants.description: Legendary restaurant in Positano with romantic sea-view tables and award-winning Italian cuisine prepared with precision and artistry. Reservations essential months in advance.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Salvatore
restaurants.description: Waterfront restaurant in Maiori featuring fresh fish bought daily from local boats and traditional cooking methods. Casual yet refined atmosphere perfect for lunch or dinner.

restaurants.name: Trattoria Gennaro
restaurants.description: Authentic neighborhood trattoria in Amalfi serving traditional dishes at local prices in a no-frills setting. Popular with residents for its value and genuine hospitality.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Furore
restaurants.description: Contemporary restaurant in Furore's hidden fjord setting with creative Mediterranean dishes and an excellent wine list featuring Campania vintages. Intimate and special-occasion worthy.
restaurants.mustTry: Swordfish with lemon and pistachio crust

activities.name: Positano Cliff Walk
activities.description: Scenic hiking trail connecting Positano to Praiano with stunning coastal views and access to secluded beaches. The path offers multiple viewpoints perfect for photography.

activities.name: Boat Tour to Capri and Blue Grotto
activities.description: Full-day guided boat excursion from Amalfi to the island of Capri featuring the famous Blue Grotto sea cave and coastal grottos. Includes swimming opportunities and lunch.

activities.name: Ravello Villa Tours and Gardens
activities.description: Explore historic clifftop villas Villa Rufolo and Villa d'Este with lush gardens, art collections, and panoramic terraces. Cultural highlight featuring medieval architecture and contemporary art installations.

activities.name: Lemon Grove Tours in Furore
activities.description: Visit traditional terraced lemon groves and learn about cultivation methods for the famous Sfusato lemons used in limoncello production. Includes tasting of limoncello and local products.

activities.name: Kayaking and Snorkeling
activities.description: Guided kayaking tour along the coast with access to hidden coves and caves for snorkeling in crystal-clear Mediterranean waters. Equipment provided and suitable for beginners.

activities.name: Cooking Class in Amalfi
activities.description: Hands-on class learning to prepare traditional pasta and regional specialties from a local chef. Includes market visit, cooking, and tasting of your creations with wine.

activities.name: Atrani Village Exploration
activities.description: Wander the smallest commune in Campania with medieval architecture, charming piazzas, and fewer tourists than Positano. Perfect for authentic photography and cultural immersion.

activities.name: Emerald Grotto Visit
activities.description: Explore the emerald-colored Grotta dello Smeraldo by boat with views of stalactites and stalagmites reflected in luminous green waters. Shorter, less crowded alternative to Blue Grotto.

activities.name: Praiano Beach and Cliff Bar Sunset
activities.description: Enjoy the small pebble beach at Praiano with local beach bars serving cocktails and fresh fish. Perfect spot to swim, relax, and watch the sunset from the water.

activities.name: Path of the Gods Trail
activities.description: Legendary hiking route from Praiano to Positano offering some of the coast's most dramatic scenery with Mediterranean vegetation and endless sea views. Moderate difficulty with excellent photo opportunities.

activities.name: Maiori Beach and Beach Club Experience
activities.description: Visit the largest beach on the Amalfi Coast with organized sections, water sports, and beachfront restaurants. Family-friendly with facilities and a more relaxed vibe than Positano.

activities.name: Ravello Concert Evening
activities.description: Attend a classical music performance or concert at Villa Rufolo's famous outdoor amphitheater with sea backdrop during summer season. World-class venue and international artists.

spots.name: Positano Main Beach Overlook
spots.description: Classic vantage point capturing the iconic stacked pastel houses cascading down the cliff face with the beach and Mediterranean Sea below.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour sunrise or sunset for warm side light on buildings

spots.name: Path of the Gods Trail Viewpoints
spots.description: Multiple scenic overlooks along the famous hiking trail with dramatic coastal landscapes, tiny villages in the distance, and layered Mediterranean vegetation.
spots.bestTime: Midday for clear visibility across the entire coast or late afternoon for warm tones

spots.name: Atrani Piazza
spots.description: Charming medieval square with weathered buildings, laundry lines, and authentic Italian village atmosphere rarely seen in touristy areas.
spots.bestTime: Early morning before crowds or late afternoon when locals gather

spots.name: Ravello Villa Rufolo Terrace
spots.description: Dramatic clifftop terraces with manicured gardens, historic architecture, and unobstructed panoramic sea views extending to Capri.
spots.bestTime: Late afternoon for warm golden light on the terraces and buildings

spots.name: Emerald Grotto Interior
spots.description: Luminous sea cave with glowing emerald water reflections on limestone walls and natural stalactite formations creating surreal compositions.
spots.bestTime: Midday when sunlight enters the cave creating maximum emerald glow effect

spots.name: Praiano Colorful Boats Harbor
spots.description: Picturesque fishing village harbor with bright traditional boats, fishing nets, and colorful buildings providing excellent street and still-life opportunities.
spots.bestTime: Early morning when fishermen are active and light is soft and directional

spots.name: Furore Fjord Hidden Beach
spots.description: Secret cove tucked into a narrow fjord with dramatic cliff walls, small beach, and weathered buildings creating an intimate composition rarely seen by tourists.
spots.bestTime: Midday when light reaches the fjord bottom, or late afternoon for dramatic cliff shadows

spots.name: Amalfi Cathedral Piazza
spots.description: Historic town square dominated by the ornate Arab-Norman cathedral with its impressive bronze doors and grand staircase, bustling with local life.
spots.bestTime: Early morning or late afternoon to avoid harsh midday shadows on the facade

spots.name: Lemon Grove Terraces
spots.description: Traditional terraced lemon groves cascading down hillsides with characteristic wooden pergolas creating geometric patterns and golden fruit highlights.
spots.bestTime: Late morning or early afternoon when sun creates strong contrast on the terraces

spots.name: Maiori Beachfront Promenade
spots.description: Long sandy beach with colorful umbrellas, beachgoers, and the backdrop of dramatic cliffs with architecture scattered up the hillside.
spots.bestTime: Golden hour for warm beach lighting and silhouettes against sea

lensRecommendations: 24-70mm f/2.8 - Versatile for landscapes, architecture, and street photography throughout the coast
70-200mm f/2.8 - Telephoto for compressed perspectives of distant villages and dramatic cliff compression
16-35mm f/2.8 - Ultra-wide for expansive coastal landscapes and dramatic cliff formations from hiking trails
50mm f/1.4 - Prime for intimate village scenes and portrait work with beautiful background separation
photography.goldenHourNotes: The Amalfi Coast's west-facing orientation makes it exceptional for sunrise shots from elevated vantage points and evening photography with warm light cascading across cliff faces. Early morning light on Positano's pastel buildings is particularly magical, while sunset illuminates the terraced landscape and sea caves with amber tones. Golden hour lasts extended periods due to the dramatic topography creating varied lighting conditions across the vertical landscape.

weather.seasonality: May through early October offers warm, dry weather ideal for hiking, boating, and exploring, with June through August being peak tourist season with temperatures reaching 26°C. October and April provide pleasant temperatures and fewer crowds, though occasional rain is possible.
weather.summary: The Amalfi Coast enjoys a Mediterranean climate with mild winters and warm, dry summers. Summer months (June-August) are hot and crowded, while spring (April-May) and fall (September-October) offer the best balance of pleasant weather and manageable tourist numbers.

hotels.name: Hostel Positano
hotels.description: Friendly hostel offering dormitory and private rooms with a social atmosphere, basic amenities, and central location in Positano near shops and restaurants.

hotels.name: Hotel Villa Franca
hotels.description: Family-run 3-star hotel with comfortable rooms, sea-view terraces, and a small beach area, featuring traditional Italian hospitality and convenient access to hiking trails.

hotels.name: Monastero Santa Maria Costantinopoli
hotels.description: Exclusive luxury hotel housed in a restored 13th-century monastery overlooking the coast, featuring suites with frescoed ceilings, Michelin-starred restaurant, and impeccable service.
